"""
Project Title: Continuous-Depth Neural ODE Classifier on MNIST (ai-ml-ds-NeuralODEMNIST2025)
File Name: continuous_depth_neural_ode_mnist.py

Short Description:
Implements a continuous-depth Neural ODE classifier in Keras + TensorFlow Probability.
Uses a learnable ODE function integrated via Dormand-Prince solver, followed by dense classification head.
"""

import os  # type: ignore
import datetime  # type: ignore
import numpy as np  # type: ignore
import tensorflow as tf  # type: ignore
import tensorflow_probability as tfp  # type: ignore
from tensorflow.keras import layers, Model, Input  # type: ignore

# ----------------------------
# 1. Hyperparameters & Setup
# ----------------------------
SEED: int = 1234
tf.random.set_seed(SEED)
np.random.seed(SEED)

BATCH_SIZE: int = 256
LR: float = 1e-3
EPOCHS: int = 20
TIME_HORIZON: tf.Tensor = tf.constant([0.0, 1.0], dtype=tf.float32)  # type: tf.Tensor
LOG_DIR: str = "./neuralode_mnist_logs/" + datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
os.makedirs(LOG_DIR, exist_ok=True)

# ----------------------------
# 2. Data Loading & Preproc
# ----------------------------
(x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test) = tf.keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()
x_train: np.ndarray = x_train.astype("float32") / 255.0
x_test: np.ndarray = x_test.astype("float32") / 255.0
x_train = x_train.reshape(-1, 28*28)
x_test = x_test.reshape(-1, 28*28)
y_train = tf.keras.utils.to_categorical(y_train, 10)
y_test = tf.keras.utils.to_categorical(y_test, 10)
train_ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((x_train, y_train)).shuffle(10000, seed=SEED).batch(BATCH_SIZE)
test_ds  = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((x_test, y_test)).batch(BATCH_SIZE)

# ----------------------------
# 3. ODE Function as Keras Layer
# ----------------------------
class ODEFunc(layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, hidden_units: int = 64):
        super().__init__()
        self.dense1 = layers.Dense(hidden_units, activation="tanh")
        self.dense2 = layers.Dense(hidden_units, activation="tanh")
        self.dense3 = layers.Dense(28*28, activation=None)
    def call(self, t, x):
        # x shape: (batch, features)
        h = self.dense1(x)
        h = self.dense2(h)
        dx = self.dense3(h)
        return dx

# ----------------------------
# 4. Neural ODE Block
# ----------------------------
class ODEBlock(layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, ode_func: ODEFunc, tol: float = 1e-6):
        super().__init__()
        self.ode_func = ode_func
        self.solver = tfp.math.ode.DormandPrince(atol=tol, rtol=tol)
    def call(self, x):
        # Integrate from t0 to t1
        results = self.solver.solve(self.ode_func, 
                                    initial_time=TIME_HORIZON[0], 
                                    initial_state=x, 
                                    solution_times=TIME_HORIZON)
        return results.states[-1]

# ----------------------------
# 5. Build Neural ODE Classifier
# ----------------------------
inp: Input = Input(shape=(28*28,), name="mnist_input")
ode_func = ODEFunc(hidden_units=128)
ode_block = ODEBlock(ode_func)
x0 = layers.Dense(128, activation="relu")(inp)
x1 = ode_block(x0)                     # continuous-depth mapping
x2 = layers.Dense(64, activation="relu")(x1)
out = layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax")(x2)
model = Model(inputs=inp, outputs=out, name="NeuralODE_MNIST")
model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(LR),
              loss="categorical_crossentropy",
              metrics=["accuracy"])
print(model.summary())

# ----------------------------
# 6. Training Loop
# ----------------------------
callbacks = [
    tf.keras.callbacks.TensorBoard(LOG_DIR),
    tf.keras.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint(LOG_DIR+"/best.h5", save_best_only=True, monitor="val_accuracy")
]
model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=test_ds, epochs=EPOCHS, callbacks=callbacks)

# ----------------------------
# 7. Example Inference Use Cases
# ----------------------------
import random  # type: ignore
def inference_examples(n: int = 5):
    idxs = random.sample(range(x_test.shape[0]), n)
    samples = x_test[idxs]
    true = np.argmax(y_test[idxs], axis=1)
    pred = np.argmax(model.predict(samples), axis=1)
    for i, t, p in zip(idxs, true, pred):
        print(f"Index {i}: True={t}, Pred={p}")

inference_examples(5)

Summary:
A Neural ODE brings continuous-depth modeling to classification tasks, integrating a learnable ODE with Keras’s GradientTape and TFP’s solver. This advanced approach suits time-series, dynamical systems, and any domain requiring flexible depth and continuous transformations—ideal for high-end research and production in AI/ML engineering. 🚀😊
